## Key Insights

1. Kharif Sowing Status: Kharif sowing data collection has started from 06 th  June, 2025 and the sowing is in preliminary stage. As on June 06 2025, the area sown under Kharif crops is 74.30 lakh ha (including 53.39 lakh ha (102% of normal area) in Sugarcane) as compared to 75.11 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.

## 2. Weather Update :

- a) Temperature: Maximum Temperatures likely  to  rise  by  2-3°C  over  Northwest  &  Central India  during  next  3  days  and  no  significant  change  thereafter.  No  significant  change  in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country.
- b) Rainfall Distribution: From June 01- 09 June, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 29% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: (-)7%; (ii) Northwest India: (-)8%; (iii) Central India: (-)48%; and South Peninsula: (-) 54%.

An  upper  air  cyclonic  circulation  lay  over  Haryana  &  neighborhood  and  another  over Southeast Himachal Pradesh & adjoining Uttarakhand in lower tropospheric levels.

A Western Disturbance lay as a cyclonic circulation over Ladakh & adjoining Kashmir in middle tropospheric levels.

Another Western Disturbance lay as a trough in middle tropospheric westerlies roughly along Long. 54°E to the north of Lat. 25°N.

Increase  in  rainfall  activity  with  Isolated  heavy  falls  very  likely  over  south  peninsular India, west coast and northeastern states from 10th June and heavy to very heavy rainfall over Karnataka and Kerala from 13 th  June.

Light/moderate rainfall  at  isolated  places  accompanied  with  thunderstorm,  lightning  & gusty winds likely over most parts of the country.

## Inputs Situation

- a) Water Reservoir Status : As on 05 th  June 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 56.80 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 31.1% of total live storage capacity (182.44 BCM). The current year's storage is nearly 138 percent of last year's storage and 129 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during  the  corresponding  period.  The  overall  storage  position  is  better than  the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.

## Rainfall Forecast:

-  Overall rainfall activity is likely to be above normal over south Peninsular India; normal to above normal over many parts of central India and below normal over northwest, east & northeast India during the week

## Advance of Southwest Monsoon:

-  The  Northern  Limit  of  Monsoon  continues  to  pass  through  17.0°N/55°E,  17.5°N/60°E, 18°N/65°E, 18.5°N/70°E, Mumbai, Ahilyanagar, Adilabad, Bhawanipatna, Puri, Sandhead Island, 23.5°N/89.5°E, Balurghat, 30°N/85°E.

## Details of each Segment

-  Southwest Monsoon likely to advance over some more parts of Central & east India during week 2 (12 to 18 June, 2025).

## Temerature

## Week 1 (06 th  - 11 th   June 2025):

-  Maximum Temperatures likely to rise by 2-3°C over Northwest & Central India during next 3 days and no significant change thereafter.
-  No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country.

## Week 2 ( 12 th  - 18 th   June 2025):

-  Maximum temperatures are likely to increase over northwest India as compared to week1. These  are  likely  to  be  above  normal  by  2-4°C  over  plains  of  northwest  India  and northeastern States; and above normal by 1-3°C over many parts of central India; and near normal or below normal over rest parts of the country during the week.
-  There is low to moderate probability of heat wave at isolated pockets of Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh during some days of the week.

## Heat Waves

-  Heat wave condition very likely at many/some places over West Rajasthan during 08 th  -11 th with severe heat wave conditions at isolated/some parts on 09 th  June.
-  Heat  wave  conditions  are  likely  to  prevail  over  Jammu-Kashmir-Ladakh-Gilgit-BaltistanMuzaffarabad  during  08 th   -10 th ,  Punjab,  Haryana,  Chandigarh  &  Delhi  during  08th-11th; south West Uttar Pradesh during 09 th  - 11 th , East Uttar Pradesh, East Rajasthan on 09 th  & 10 th , north Madhya Pradesh on 10 th  & 11 th  June.

## 4. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION

## (a) Soil Moisture Observation

-  Soil moisture during 29 May - 04 June 2025 is better to the average of the past 9 years in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, Western M.P, Maharashtra, Karnataka, A.P., Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Assam and Chhattisgarh.
-  Similar to average of past 9 years average in Punjab, West and Central U.P and Eastern M.P.
-  Whereas lower than average of past 9 years avg. in Bihar and Eastern UP.

## Kharif Crops - Area coverage

Key Insights

1. Kharif Sowing Status: Kharif sowing data collection has started from 06 th  June, 2025 and the sowing is in preliminary stage. As on June 06 2025, the area sown under Kharif crops is 74.30 lakh ha (including 53.39 lakh ha (102% of normal area) in Sugarcane) as compared to 75.11 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.

2. Weather Update :

- a) Temperature: Maximum Temperatures likely  to  rise  by  2-3°C  over  Northwest  &  Central India  during  next  3  days  and  no  significant  change  thereafter.  No  significant  change  in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country.
- b) Rainfall Distribution: From June 01- 09 June, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 29% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: (-)7%; (ii) Northwest India: (-)8%; (iii) Central India: (-)48%; and South Peninsula: (-) 54%.

An  upper  air  cyclonic  circulation  lay  over  Haryana  &  neighborhood  and  another  over Southeast Himachal Pradesh & adjoining Uttarakhand in lower tropospheric levels.

A Western Disturbance lay as a cyclonic circulation over Ladakh & adjoining Kashmir in middle tropospheric levels.

Another Western Disturbance lay as a trough in middle tropospheric westerlies roughly along Long. 54°E to the north of Lat. 25°N.

Increase  in  rainfall  activity  with  Isolated  heavy  falls  very  likely  over  south  peninsular India, west coast and northeastern states from 10th June and heavy to very heavy rainfall over Karnataka and Kerala from 13 th  June.

Light/moderate rainfall  at  isolated  places  accompanied  with  thunderstorm,  lightning  & gusty winds likely over most parts of the country.

Inputs Situation

- a) Water Reservoir Status : As on 05 th  June 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 56.80 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 31.1% of total live storage capacity (182.44 BCM). The current year's storage is nearly 138 percent of last year's storage and 129 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during  the  corresponding  period.  The  overall  storage  position  is  better than  the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.

-  No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country.

An upper air cyclonic circulation lay over Haryana & neighborhood and another over Southeast Himachal Pradesh & adjoining Uttarakhand in lower tropospheric levels. Another Western Disturbance lay as a trough in middle tropospheric westerlies roughly along Long. 54°E to the north of Lat. 25°N. Increase in rainfall activity with Isolated heavy falls very likely over south peninsular India, west coast and northeastern states from 10th June and heavy to very heavy rainfall over Karnataka and Kerala from 13th June. Light/moderate rainfall at isolated places accompanied with thunderstorm, lightning & gusty winds likely over most parts of the country.
